example.problem: You took A (3 credits), B+ (4 credits), A- (3 credits) and B (3 credits). What is your GPA?
steps: Convert each grade to points: A = 4.0, B+ = 3.3, A- = 3.7, B = 3.0.
example.title: One semester, four courses

faqs.a: For most undergraduate programs, 3.5 and above is strong, 3.0 is solid, and below 2.0 risks academic probation. Graduate schools and competitive scholarships often expect 3.5+. Always check your own school's requirements.
A+ is usually capped at 4.0 in the standard scale, the same as A. Some high schools weight honors or AP classes above 4.0, but most college scales treat A+ as 4.0. You can just enter it as A here.

GPA is a weighted average: each grade's points are multiplied by the course's credits, so a 4-credit B+ (13.2 points) counts more than a 3-credit B+ (9.9 points). Averaging the grades directly would ignore the credit hours.
faqs.q: Why is GPA weighted by credits instead of a simple average?

faqs.a: No. Different schools use different scales, some weight honors classes, and some exclude pass/fail or repeated courses. This calculator follows the common unweighted 4.0 scale, which is a good estimate but not a replacement for your official transcript.
faqs.q: Is this exactly how my school calculates GPA?

howItWorks: Your GPA is a weighted average. Each letter grade converts to a number of grade points on the standard 4.0 scale, and each course's points are multiplied by its credit hours. The calculator adds up all the grade points, adds up all the credits, and divides the two totals.

The weighting matters: a 4-credit B+ contributes 13.2 grade points while a 3-credit B+ contributes only 9.9, so heavier courses pull your GPA more. This follows the common unweighted 4.0 scale as a good estimate; your school's official scale may differ, for example by weighting honors classes or excluding pass/fail courses.
intro: Work out your grade point average on the standard 4.0 scale. Type one course per line as a letter grade followed by its credit hours, like "A 3", and the calculator does the weighted average for you.

mistakes.text: GPA is a weighted average, not a simple one. A (4.0), B+ (3.3), A- (3.7) and B (3.0) do not average to 3.5 unless every course has the same credits.
mistakes.title: Averaging the grades directly

mistakes.text: A B+ is 3.3 grade points, not 3.5, and a B- is 2.7, not 2.5. The plus and minus steps on the standard scale are about 0.3, and using the wrong values shifts your GPA.
mistakes.title: Treating B+ as 3.5

mistakes.text: Schools usually exclude pass/fail courses from GPA. Only include courses with letter grades, or your average will be pulled down by courses that should not count.
mistakes.title: Including pass/fail courses

mistakes.text: If you write "3 A" instead of "A 3", the line will not parse. The grade comes first, then the credit hours.
mistakes.title: Writing credits before the grade
